quote: No. I I I wasn't interested in that. So I already had the the discount, and then that's something that's trying to find out how much was it and everything.
stewart_read: Customer discloses he already had 'the discount' — implying prior contact with Ion or a competitor — and the rep never asks who offered it or what it entailed.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged this too minor/garbled to chase given the customer's own broken phrasing, choosing to keep the call moving rather than risk confusion.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to ask one clarifying follow-up ('who gave you that discount, and was that recent?') — costs 10 seconds, gives the closer competitive context.

quote: Yeah. Okay. Gotcha. So you're just kinda curious to see what the incentives and everything looked like?
stewart_read: Rep flattens a specific, slightly confusing customer answer into a generic incentive-curiosity label rather than reflecting back what he actually said as a hook to build on.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as reasonable active-listening paraphrase rather than a missed hook, since the customer's own words were unclear.
coaching_implication: Encourage reps to hold open the ambiguity ('what discount were you looking at before?') rather than resolving it into the nearest script bucket.

stewart_read: Rep unilaterally introduces 'your wife' inside the credit qualifier line without ever having asked or confirmed a co-owner earlier — the actual co-owner question at 01:19 got only a non-answer ('It's been a while'). The transcript's customer response here is also unclear, so this is a co-owner-confirmation gap rather than a spouse-objection-handling moment.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have prior file data indicating a spouse exists, making this a reasonable shorthand rather than an assumption; transcript does not resolve this either way.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to close the loop explicitly on co-owner status before assuming a spouse in a later line — don't let 'it's been a while' pass as an answer to a required verify item.

quote: So I do have you here, John, as the property owner. Is there anyone else on the title of the home with you at all?
stewart_read: The customer's transcribed reply, 'It's been a while,' does not answer the co-owner question at all — it reads as a non-sequitur or ASR garble — yet the rep proceeds to the next verify item without re-asking or confirming.
alternative_hypothesis: The transcript itself may be unreliable here (crossed lines / ASR error), so this could be a transcription artifact rather than the rep truly skipping a real answer.
coaching_implication: Flag for the manager that this exchange is not clean evidence of a rep miss — but coach the rep on the general habit of re-confirming when a verify answer doesn't logically match the question asked.

quote: I would say about 3¢ a month.
stewart_read: This figure is almost certainly an ASR mis-transcription of a dollar amount (the rep's 'Oh my goodness' and follow-up 'up there in 3 hundreds' suggest the real number was likely $300+), not a literal three-cent bill. Treat the number itself as unreliable; only the rep's and customer's reactions are usable evidence.
alternative_hypothesis: If taken literally, this would be a trivial bill with no pain to anchor — but that contradicts the rep's audible surprise, making the literal reading implausible.
coaching_implication: This limits how confidently the manager can use this call as a bill-anchor example; treat the underlying dollar figure as unconfirmed rather than a coachable number.

quote: K. Well, yeah, that's pretty much all the questions I have here for you, John.
stewart_read: After the bill reaction at 02:39, the rep never returns to it — no flip into 'that's exactly the kind of bill solar could take a bite out of,' just a transition into bill collection mechanics.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be deliberately saving the emotional pitch for after the actual bill document is collected, since panel sizing requires the real usage data — a strategic sequencing choice rather than an omission.
coaching_implication: Even if sequencing is intentional, a one-line bridge ('based on what you're telling me, this could make a real difference') costs nothing and keeps the emotional thread alive into bill collection.

quote: Yeah. I could give you a call kinda tomorrow in the morning if that works good for you, and we can just get the rest of the information we need.
stewart_read: No specific time is locked ('tomorrow in the morning' is not a time), no handshake confirmation, and no button-up elements (text follow-up, hour block, no-driving instruction) are present.
alternative_hypothesis: Because this is a self-callback rather than a closer appointment, the full button-up script may not strictly apply — but a specific time window would still improve show-probability.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to always lock a specific time window even for internal callbacks — 'tomorrow morning' invites no-shows on both sides.
